general_information.Description: 1. Course Objectives: After completing this course, students will be able to: - Comprehend the evolving relationship between financial technology (FinTech) and managerial applications, analyzing how technological advancements reshape financial decision-making and business strategies. - Identify key challenges and opportunities that traditional financial institutions and businesses face in adapting to fintech innovations. - Evaluate the role of fintech solutions in enhancing operational efficiency, reducing costs, and driving strategic decision-making in financial management. - Apply insights from The FINTECH Book to real-world business scenarios, assessing the implications of financial disintermediation and digital transformation. 2. Course Content: Regulatory frameworks and challenges for financial institutions; the emergence and impact of fintech disruptors; technological innovation in financial services; financial disintermediation and its broader economic implications. 3. Activities and Teaching Methodology: The course combines engaging lectures, real-world case studies on fintech innovations, interactive group discussions, and hands-on projects that analyze the transformative impact of technology on financial systems.
general_information.StudentTasks: '- Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination - Actively participate in class activities - Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class - Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose - Read the textbook in advance - Access the course website (http://flm.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students and for practicing and assessment.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Understand FinTech Ecosystem and Trends; identify key players, components, and trends shaping the fintech industry.
Analyze and evaluate fintech innovations and their effectiveness in driving social and financial inclusion.
Explore and analyze successful fintech hubs and understand funding mechanisms and investment trends.
Examine enterprise strategies and lessons from successful and failed fintech ventures.
Explain Blockchain principles and predict emerging fintech trends and disruptions.
Develop the ability to critically analyze fintech case studies and real-world applications.
Apply theoretical knowledge to practical scenarios through assignments and case studies.
Cultivate teamwork and independent working skills with a high sense of responsibility and professionalism.

assessments.Note: Option 1: Participation scores will be given based on students' class attendance, preparation, quantity as well as quality of participation in classroom; quality of participation is demonstrated through asking relevant questions, making statements that add to and facilitate class discussions, and building upon others’ comments. Class participation accounts for 14% of the final score. Option 2 (For Constructivism Approach only): Follow lecturer's proposal

assessments.Duration: OP1: Report and Presentation in class (end of the course); OP2 (For Constructivism Approach only): Follow lecturer's proposal
assessments.Question Type: OP1: Suggestion: Choose a specific FinTech innovation or trend to analyze. Possible topics include: Blockchain and Cryptocurrencies, Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in FinTech, Digital Banking and Neobanks, Peer-to-Peer Lending, Robo-Advisors, RegTech (Regulatory Technology), InsurTech (Insurance Technology); OP2 (For Constructivism Approach only): Follow lecturer's proposal

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: OP1: Thinking creatively, making decisions, solving problems,Personal qualities: Individual responsibility, self-esteem, sociability, self-management, and integrity. OP2 (For Constructivism Approach only): Follow lecturer's proposal
